evidence.quote: EIR is a well-documented but often under-recognized condition, particularly in individuals engaging in unaccustomed or excessive physical activity. The pathophysiology involves muscle injury leading to the release of intracellular contents, including myoglobin, which can cause AKI due to tubular obstruction and direct toxicity. Primary factors that caused EIR in our case include poor body fitness combined with prolonged-duration, high-intensity, and weight-bearing exercises, together with other predisposing factors, which included dehydration and a hot environment.^(,)

summary.text: A 31-year-old female army trainee without significant medical history developed malaise, muscle aches, severe headache and subjective fevers after intensive exercise, with dark urine48hours after training. She denied recent viral/GI illness, prescribed medications/statins, herbal/traditional remedies, prior muscle symptoms and suggestive personal/family myopathy history. Authors describe poor fitness, prolonged high-intensity weight-bearing exercise, dehydration and a hot environment as contributors.

On day3 at the previous facility, creatinine544.9µmol/L and BUN13.1mmol/L were elevated, hemoglobin8.1g/dL and total protein59.5g/L low, and ALT195U/L/AST238U/L elevated, with+++RBC urinalysis; initial albumin results were unreported. IV hydration preceded transfer on day7. Repeat creatinine271µmol/L and hemoglobin9.2g/dL improved. BUN6.08mmol/L, protein71.5g/L, albumin45.5g/L, ALT40U/L, AST20U/L, GGT and electrolytes were described as normal/normalized. Day7 urine retained+RBCs; hepatitisB/C serology was negative.

Rhabdomyolysis with AKI was diagnosed clinically; CK testing was unavailable at both facilities and serum myoglobin/LDH were not assessed, limiting specificity. Infectious/metabolic causes were considered less likely without definitive assays. No myoglobinuria is inferred from dark urine and RBC positivity. Hydration led to recovery without dialysis. Discharge occurred on an unspecified day; two weeks later she was asymptomatic with normalized renal and liver panels.
